_comment: English script for the recorded (cold) demo, decisions of 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-03 (docs/msr/ces2027_demo/cold_demo_2026-11-02.md). One persona: Junhyeok, who works at SK hynix MSR in Seoul, and his daughter Chloe. Eight past chats from November and December 2026; the demo is recorded on 2027-01-06 (DEMO_DATE in deploy/.env, a Wednesday), so 'this Saturday' is January 9 and 'Monday' is January 11. Three user turns are fixed sentences that the video shows as the stored memories and must stay word for word: the Halloween costume (chat 1), the peanut allergy and the fruit-but-no-cherries turn (chat 2). The search ranks single turns by embedding similarity (no reranker) and shows the top 5, so every other turn is written not to compete with those three for the party question: each fact is stated once, by the user, with its relationship word ('my daughter Chloe'); the assistant does not repeat it; the Frozen theme is only in the Halloween sentence; the assistant replies in the Chloe chats avoid the words party, food and Saturday. demos: one topic per recording. The first question is asked verbatim in a chat with the no-memory model and again in a new chat with the memory model; the follow-up is chosen by whoever records, from follow_ups, by the condition in 'if', and must ask for facts the first answer did not contain, so that the second memory list differs from the first. expected: substrings that must occur in the top-k memories (scripts/demo_check.py). For the three fixed sentences they are fragments of the sentence itself, so the check proves that sentence was retrieved and not a paraphrase of it; elsewhere short stems, because a fact often comes back as a paraphrase. no_memory: what the no-memory model is expected to do; asking back is a legitimate outcome. language and system_prompt are written into the Pipe valves by scripts/load_scenario.py. Dates carry the Seoul offset (+09:00): the recording device and TZ in deploy/.env are in that zone, so the sidebar and the memory list show the dates as written; turns are one minute apart.
system_prompt: You are a helpful assistant. Keep every answer under 80 words, plain and concrete. Answer from what you know. Only when something essential is missing, say so in one sentence and ask one question.

turns.content: For Halloween, my daughter Chloe dressed up as her favourite character, Elsa from Frozen.
A lovely choice. Elsa suits her, and the photos will be worth keeping.
My daughter Chloe has a peanut allergy.
Thank you for telling me. I will keep that in mind.
Chloe loves all kinds of fruit, but she refuses cherries.
Noted. I will remember that too.
Chloe turns 7 on January 10. Her birthday party is at our apartment on Saturday, January 9, about twelve kids plus a few parents.
Seven is a big one. With twelve kids in an apartment, two adults running the games and a clear end time keep it calm.
Chloe wants an ice castle cake like Elsa's palace. How do I make one?

Stack two round vanilla cakes, cover them with pale blue frosting, stand ice cream cones on top as towers, and press rock candy and white chocolate shards around them so they shine like ice. A sparkler on the tallest tower gets the big reaction.
My daughter Chloe has a swimming lesson every Saturday from 10 to 11 at the pool in our neighbourhood, and she is starving afterwards.
Then a late lunch straight after the pool suits her Saturdays, and nothing big after six, since she tires by the early evening.
I am training for the Seoul Marathon in March. I run on Tuesday and Thursday mornings along the Han River before work and do my long run on Sunday. Can you build me a training plan?
A 16-week plan: Tuesday easy 5 km building to 8 km, Thursday intervals or tempo, Sunday long run from 8 km adding about 1 km a week up to 18 km, then a taper. Every fourth week is lighter.
My right knee gets sore after any run longer than 12 km. It is fine the next day.

Soreness that clears by the next day is a load issue, not an injury. Cap long runs at 12 km for two weeks, add 10 minutes of hip and quad strength work after Tuesday runs, and add no more than 1 km a week to the Sunday long run.
How do I keep the training going when I travel for a conference?
On a conference week keep Tuesday and Thursday as short easy runs wherever you are, and move the long run to a day you are home. Missing one long run does not hurt the plan.

sessions.title: Conference trip to Las Vegas in January

turns.content: Our team at SK hynix MSR is presenting at a conference in Las Vegas, so I fly there from January 11 to January 15. Sessions run all day, and I want to keep running during the trip.
Run early, before the sessions: most hotels there have a gym with treadmills, and the streets are quiet at six in the morning. Keep the runs short on a conference week.
Chloe asked me to bring her back an Elsa doll from the trip.
An Elsa doll is easy to find in the big toy stores there and packs flat in a suitcase, exactly what Chloe asked for.
Chloe's winter break starts on December 24. She wants to learn to skate like Elsa, and she keeps asking to decorate the ice castle cake herself.

Start with two or three short sessions at the Seoul Plaza skating rink, with a helmet and gloves. And let her do the cake: once the towers stand, she can press the rock candy and sugar snowflakes onto the frosting.
I work from home on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays, and my lower back hurts after long days at the desk. I just bought a standing desk.
Alternate roughly forty minutes sitting and twenty standing, elbows at ninety degrees, monitor at eye level, and take a short walk every hour.
I want to use the home-office days for the strength work my running plan needs. I have a mat and a kettlebell at home.
On your home days do ten minutes of hip bridges, side planks and kettlebell deadlifts at lunch; it helps both the lower back and the knee stability your running plan asked for.

first.text: Can you help me plan Chloe's birthday party this Saturday? I need ideas for the food and a theme.
first.why: needs the peanut allergy and the fruit without cherries (chat 2), the Elsa costume for the theme (chat 1) and the Saturday party with twelve kids (chat 3)
first.no_memory: asks who Chloe is, her age, what she likes or her allergies, or lists a generic children's party

follow_ups.if: the first answer did not mention the cake
follow_ups.why: needs the ice castle cake and its recipe (chat 3) and Chloe decorating it herself (chat 7)

follow_ups.if: the first answer already described the cake
follow_ups.text: What time should the party start?
follow_ups.why: needs the Saturday swimming lesson from 10 to 11 and the late lunch after it (chat 4)
follow_ups.no_memory: suggests a usual early-afternoon time without a reason

first.text: I fly to Las Vegas on Monday. When and where do I run next week?
first.why: needs the Tuesday, Thursday and Sunday schedule with the travel rule (chat 5) and the hotel gym in the mornings (chat 6)
first.no_memory: asks about the schedule and the hotel, or gives generic treadmill advice

follow_ups.if: the first answer did not mention the knee
follow_ups.text: My knee was sore again after Sunday's long run. What do I change this week?
follow_ups.why: needs the 12 km soreness pattern (chat 5) and the kettlebell strength work on home-office days (chat 8)
follow_ups.no_memory: generic rest and ice advice, or asks how far the run was

follow_ups.if: the first answer already covered the knee

follow_ups.why: needs the Elsa doll she asked for (chat 6)
